page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i4.xlarge is an x86_64 instance type belonging to the Local SSDs family, deployed on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz, delivering 4 dedicated vCPUs without shared resource contention. The system includes 32.0 GB of RAM, establishing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Discrete hardware accelerators such as GPUs are not present in this configuration.

A central architectural feature of the instance is its local storage configuration, which provides a dedicated 959 GB SSD. This local solid-state capacity delivers direct-attached disk access compared to network-based storage volumes, though applications must account for instance-tied disk life cycles. Baseline network bandwidth is provisioned at 4 Gbps, and the configuration includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating VPC-level egress configurations or Elastic IP bindings for external network communication.

Given its combination of generous memory capacity, dedicated CPU cores, and direct-attached storage, the ecs.i4.xlarge exhibits a balanced hardware profile for memory-sensitive and I/O-heavy operations. The instance is suited for relational database management systems, transactional key-value stores, distributed caches, search indexing engines, and real-time operational data processing workloads.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i4.xlarge is an instance within the Local SSDs family configured for storage- and memory-focused enterprise workloads. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed by KVM, the system is driven by a 2.7 GHz Intel Xeon 8369B processor featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8.0 GB memory-to-core ratio, and integrates 959 GB of dedicated local SSD storage. Network connectivity is maintained via a 4 Gbps baseline network interface, while no discrete GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provisioned. The high memory density combined with direct-attached local solid-state capacity makes the ecs.i4.xlarge suited for I/O-intensive workloads, including transactional databases, operational data stores, distributed caching layers, and search indexing services that require dependable computing cores and low storage latency.
